Leibniz thinks that, even we can explain the existence of each of the geometry books by the one from which it was copied, we can’t explain why these books exist at all.

And what goes for the geometry books, Leibniz thinks, goes for the world as a whole. Even if we can explain every state of the world in terms of the preceding state of the world, we lack an explanation of the fact that there is a world at all.
